BLOCK.why: Claude Code's hook protocol defines exit 2 as block, so every refusal in a hook entry point is a block and it has no separate usage code: a hook that cannot parse its input fails closed (host ruling relayed by github-8f, 2026-10-15)

DEFER.why: a precondition is unmet and nothing ran; a later attempt may succeed. A lock held by another LIVE holder is this (the holder will finish).

CANNOT_RUN.why: an instrument fault: the tool, check or witness could not evaluate (ruff or mypy cannot run, a witness cannot reach its target, an unsound contract), so the result is UNKNOWN. Never read as success, never retried as if a precondition might clear; it surfaces as an instrument problem. A unit may still list 7 in SuccessExitStatus when its run record carries it and its stall alert reads it: that is a unit-level choice, not a verdict change (host ruling relayed by github-8f, 2026-10-15, after luthen's apply_converge case).

IDLE.why: the idle-session watchdog's alarm: a session went quiet past its learned limit while ready cards waited, and the process exits so the harness tells the session (operator ask relayed by github-8f, 2026-10-17; mtools:W1474). Not a failure of the watchdog.
